messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Sampling from posterior
parts:
On Mon, 2012-03-26 at 16:12 +0200, Virgilio Gómez Rubio wrote:
> Hi,
>
> Is there any way of sampling from the joint posterior of the fitted
> values with INLA? I guess the answer is no but I am
> not sure. Alternatively, is there any way of computing how likely a
> new dataset is given a fitted model?

this topic has been discussed several times, at least internally. so,
what is there now, is a prototype:

inla.hyperpar.sampler(result)

that will sample from the joint of the hyperparameters, either in the
internal or user-scale. its currently undocumented, but as said, its a
prototype only, and it might change, as we're not sure what we really
want/need in this direction.

when you say 'sampling from the joint posterior'; its indeed possible
but not yet implemented. its not awfully hard to add, its just
administration mainly.

there are two strategies to provide samples. do we want samples for both
the hyperparameters (theta) and the latent field (x), as

1. for each theta-configuration used in the numerical integration,
provide N samples from x.

or

2. sample theta from its marginal and then for each theta-configuration,
sample a realisation of x.

?

option 1, can be done with mainly with no cost at all, as long as its
done in the same call, like

result = inla(..., control.compute=list(nsamples = 100))

say [THIS IS JUST AN EXAMPLE!]

whereas option 2, would require a new run, and can be done after, like

result = inla(...)
my.samples = inla.sample(result, nsamples = 100)

and would cost quite a lot compared to option 1.

option 1, has also the benefite, that we could correct samples using
their marginals, so we're using a Gaussian copula and correct with the
computed marginals. whereas option 2, the same idea would be costly, as
we do not want to recompute the marginals and only the mixture is
stored, so with option 2 we're ending up sampling just the Gaussian's.

any ideas ?
